answer: A lagoon glassworks stays honest when every new identity must hand-grind a distinct prism that splits one signal beam into a spectrum no other prism repeats, and a distinct master glassworker certifies the cut under lamplight. The first fake owes one prism, the second two, the third four, doubling each time, so the tenth fake alone owes 512 prisms and twenty fakes would owe over a million. Bulk farming fails because grinding one prism takes a full day of steady hands, and one worker cannot polish a thousand lenses at once, like a lagoon that reflects one sky per still surface.
